_prototype_verification: PROTOTYPE rule pack. Tier 1 county parameters reflect publicly documented Georgia Jobs Tax Credit values; verify all numbers (per-job amount, thresholds, county designations, benefit period, carryforward) against current Georgia Department of Revenue guidance before any real client use.

credit.name: Georgia Jobs Tax Credit
credit.summary: Statutory credit for net new full-time jobs. This pack prices the $3,500 / 2-job designation band — Tier 1 Bottom-40 county, Military Zone or Opportunity Zone — which is open to ANY lawful business. Standard Tier 1-4 ($4,000/$3,000/$1,750/$1,250, 2/10/15/25 jobs) is restricted to Eligible Business Enterprises and is NOT modelled here. Source: the partner's methodology team, 10 Sep 2026.

tax_year_convention.label: begins
tax_year_convention._note: Georgia labels a tax year by the year it BEGINS: a fiscal year opening in April 2024 is Tax Year 2024. The common business convention labels a fiscal year by the year it ENDS. The two agree only for calendar-year filers. READ FROM THE REGULATION, NOT YET CONFIRMED BY THE PARTNER - see PILOT-07. The certified reference run is consistent with this reading: its window opens 2023-07-28 and the whole project calls it TY2023.

filing.window: With Georgia Form IT-CA at return filing
filing.filing_channel: Georgia Tax Center (GTC) e-file or with the paper return
filing.deadline_note: File with the original Georgia income-tax return for the tax year (including extensions).
required_attachments: Form IT-CA with per-county net-new job counts
Average Monthly Headcount schedule (base year vs credit year)
Payroll register / evidence pack supporting the One/Zero calculation
County tier designation reference for the credit year
filing._note: Prototype filing guidance for demonstration. Confirm the exact GA DOR form edition, e-file path, and attachment list with the partner (PILOT-06) before any real filing.

seasonal_conditions._note: The workbook states that a full-time job filled by a seasonal employee is eligible when the job otherwise meets program requirements. The Reference source has no employment-type field, so this condition is metadata only until supplied.

staffing_entity_conditions._note: The Reference source lacks staffing/client-industry fields; do not infer this classification.

geographic_scope._note: GA eligibility is decided at the LOCATION, not by the company NAICS code (confirmed with the partner's team, 10 Sep 2026). Eight designations exist: T1/T2/T3/T4 at $4,000/$3,000/$1,750/$1,250 for Eligible Business Enterprises only, plus T1B40/MZ/OZ at $3,500 and LDCT at $3,500 (5 jobs). This prototype prices every GA worksite in the $3,500 / 2-job band, which is the one open to any lawful business — including the retail and food-service clients in the demo set, which cannot access standard Tier 1. Production must load the annual DOR designation list AND a per-worksite Eligible Business Enterprise flag.

headcount_formula._note: Average monthly FTE is computed as sum(hours_in_month) / (4.33 * fte_basis_hours_per_week) per employee, then summed across qualifying employees. This is the PROTOTYPE quick-estimate metric; the statutory engine is the one_zero block below.

one_zero._doc_source: the product's documented One/Zero methodology (Pay Period Method, Min Max Method, and the BCS business-framing overview, 2024)

pay_code_policy._note: CALC-11: Georgia uses ALL REMUNERATION for the weekly-wage test (Regular + Overtime + Bonus + Commission). Non-wage pay codes (mileage / expense reimbursements) are suppressed. Base-pay-only states would exclude Overtime/Bonus. The synthetic dataset is Regular-only, so suppression is a no-op on the demo numbers; proven on a dedicated fixture. Confirm the GA eligible-code list with the partner (PILOT-05).

one_zero._note: GA JTC Base Calculation: per-employee weekly avg hours >= 35 AND weekly avg wages >= the resolved annual floor. Headcount is tested at unit/worksite grain and averaged over monthly counts. Historical table: 2024=$686; 2025=$680.

calculation.threshold_offset_note: Per OCGA § 48-7-40 the first 2 net new jobs (Tier 1) do not qualify; we subtract that threshold from qualifying FTE before applying the per-job amount.
